attempts.raw_response: Make sure the post is sturdy and at least 10 feet tall, and consider mounting it in a spot that gets at least 6–8 hours of direct sunlight each day, especially in cooler climates. Bats prefer warm, stable roosts, so avoid placing the house near bright outdoor lights or in heavily shaded areas. Ideally, face the bat house south or southeast to capture morning sun. Also, ensure there is a clear flight path with no obstructions like tree branches or power lines within 20 feet of the entrance. Once installed, be patient—it may take a season or two for bats to discover and occupy the house.

pair.human_continuation: Make sure to use a post that is 13 to 15 feet (4.0 to 4.6 m) long so that it will still be at more than 10 to 12 feet (3.0 to 3.7 m) high once one end is buried in the ground. If you are using a wooden post, wrap it with a piece of sheet metal 18 inches (46 cm) high roughly 3 feet (0.91 m) off of the ground. This will stop predators from being able to climb the post. Bats are nocturnal, meaning they’ll nest in the bat house during the day and fly at night. In order to avoid disturbing them during the day or confusing them when it’s nighttime, make sure the location you pick is away from any artificial lighting.
pair.prefix: Pick a location on a wall of your home that is at least 10 feet (3.0 m) off of the ground to hang your bat house.  Putting the bat house high off the ground also helps prevent predators on the ground, such as cats and dogs, from being able to hunt the bats. If you can't find a perfect location on a pre-existing wall, you can erect a post in your yard to hang the bat house from.
